transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just here because... well, my family thinks I'm making things up. But I know what I see. The people from the hospital, and some folks from the cleaning agency where I work... they've been watching our house. They even follow my cleaning routes. I think they're trying to see if I'm taking proper care of my husband.
When you think about people watching your house and following your cleaning routes, do you have any doubt that this is actually happening, or are you completely certain about it?

Like I said... I know what I see. 

Everyone keeps acting like I'm just imagining it, but I'm not. I'm certain the hospital people and the ones from the agency are watching my routes to check on how I care for my husband. I don't have any doubts about it.

Besides the people watching you and following your cleaning routes, do you experience other unusual things — like hearing voices, or having thoughts that seem to come from outside your mind, or noticing that people can read your thoughts?

I don't know about people reading my thoughts. But... sometimes I hear things. 

When it's quiet at the house, I'll hear this woman's voice. She's usually near the kitchen window. She tells me to check the locks, or... or to move his pills. It's not in my head, though. It sounds just like she's standing right there.
When did you first start hearing this woman's voice — was that before you noticed people watching your house, or did the watching start first?
I don't know exactly which was first. They both... it's been about 11 months now. Since the voice and the watching started.
Over these 11 months, have the voice and the watching been happening pretty much all the time, or do they come and go?
Pretty much... all the time. The voice and... knowing they're watching us. It's just been happening for about 11 months now.

Before these 11 months started, did you notice any gradual changes in how you were thinking or feeling — like becoming more suspicious of people, or having trouble concentrating — or did the voice and the watching start pretty suddenly?
I don't really know. I don't think I noticed anything different before that. It just... it just started happening.
During these 11 months, have there been any times — even a few days or a week — when the voice went away or the watching seemed to stop, or has it been pretty constant the whole time?
I don't think so. It's just... it's been there the whole time, I guess. I haven't noticed it stop.
When the woman's voice tells you to move your husband's pills, do you actually do what she says, or do you resist it?
I... I don't really want to talk about that. I just... I hear her. That's all.
Have you been able to go to work and take care of your husband's daily needs during these 11 months, or has the voice and the watching made it hard for you to do those things?

It's... it's been hard. My agency, they... they took away my supervisory routes. People were complaining. Said they couldn't rely on me like before. And at home... I guess I haven't been doing everything I should. My husband and our pastor, they've had to help out more... just to keep things going. I just... I can't keep up with it all right now.
Before these 11 months ago when the voice and watching started, have you ever had experiences like this in the past — hearing voices or feeling like people were watching or following you?
No. I don't... I don't remember anything like that before. It's just been recently.

You mentioned the voice and the watching have been there the whole time for these 11 months. But I want to ask: have there been any days or weeks where you felt more like yourself — where the voice seemed quieter or less real, or where you felt less worried about being watched?

I suppose... there was a little while. Maybe a few weeks where it was a bit quieter. I was sleeping more then... just not rushing around as much. But... it didn't go away. I still heard her by the kitchen window. And I still knew the agency was watching us. That hasn't stopped.
During those few weeks when things were quieter and you were sleeping more — during that time, did the voice completely go away, or was it still there but just quieter?

No, it... it didn't go away. Like I said, it was just... quieter for a few weeks. When I was sleeping more. But... I still heard her. By the window. And I still knew they were watching. It never stopped.

You mentioned a few weeks where things were quieter and you were sleeping more — during that entire time, did you feel back to normal, or did you still feel something was wrong even though the voice was quieter?

I didn't feel normal, no. I... I think I just said that. It was just a quieter spell for those few weeks. I was sleeping more, not rushing around as much. But... I still heard her by the kitchen window. And I still believed the agency was watching us. So... no.

When you were sleeping more during those few weeks and things were quieter — thinking back on it now, would you say that period lasted just a few weeks, or did it go on for a couple of months or longer?

Just several weeks. Not months. I... I feel like I just said this. It was just a quieter spell. I was sleeping more, not rushing around as much. But I still heard the voice by the kitchen window. And I still believed the agency was watching us. That's all it was.

When you think about everything that's been happening over these 11 months — the voice, the watching, not being able to keep up at work and at home — which one bothers you the most or seems like the biggest problem to you right now?

I don't really know... I guess work. The cleaning agency took away my supervisory routes. They said... clients and the other girls said they couldn't rely on my work like they used to. That bothers me. And... I suppose at home, too. My husband and our pastor have had to step in a lot more. Because I'm... I guess they think I'm not keeping up with the caregiving and the household stuff safely. So... probably that.

Looking back over these 11 months, was there ever a stretch of time — even just 2 weeks or so — when you didn't hear the woman's voice at all and you weren't worried about being watched, where everything felt completely normal again?

No... I don't think so. I mean, I... I thought I just explained this part. There wasn't a time where it all stopped. The voices and... that feeling that people are watching us... it's been happening for about 11 months now. Just... the whole time.

I want to make sure I understand the timeline correctly. Over these 11 months, has there been any stretch of time — even 2 weeks or so — when both the voice completely stopped AND you felt confident the watching had ended, where you felt like things were back to normal?
I... I just said this. No. There wasn't any time like that. The voices and... that feeling about people watching us... it's just been going on for the whole 11 months. It hasn't stopped.
When the woman's voice tells you to move your husband's pills or check the locks, have you actually followed those instructions and done what she tells you to do?
I... well, I don't know. I mean... sometimes. I guess sometimes I do what she says. Just to... just to be safe.

If I told you that I checked with the hospital and the cleaning agency, and they said they are NOT watching your house or following your cleaning routes, would that change what you believe, or would you still be certain they are watching you?

I... I don't know what they told you. But people keep acting like I'm just imagining it all. I know what's happening. The hospital people, some of the folks from the agency... they've been watching the house. Watching my routes. They want to see if I'm taking proper care of him. So... no. It wouldn't change anything. I know what I know.

The hospital people, some of the folks from the agency... they've been watching the house. Watching my routes. They want to see if I'm taking proper care of him. So... no. It wouldn't change anything. I know what I know.

opening_question.intent: Establish rapport and identify the chief complaint that brings the patient to psychiatric evaluation
opening_question.question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient presents with a clear psychotic disorder characterized by prominent delusions (organized surveillance by hospital and agency staff) and auditory hallucinations (woman's voice by kitchen window) persisting for 11 months with continuous presence. Symptoms have caused significant functional impairment (loss of supervisory duties at work, increased dependence on family for household and caregiving tasks). The delusions are fixed and resistant to contradictory evidence. While there was a brief period of reduced symptom intensity (several weeks with more sleep, quieter voice), the core psychotic symptoms never fully remitted and the patient never felt completely normal. The continuous course with functional decline, combined with prominent hallucinations and delusions, is most consistent with Paranoid Schizophrenia (F20.0) rather than other psychotic disorders. The patient demonstrates some insight limitation (refusing to acknowledge the possibility that beliefs are false) and possible command hallucination compliance ("sometimes I do what she says").

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms present for 11 months with continuous course; no symptom-free periods lasting 2 weeks or longer; meets duration criterion for schizophrenia (1 month of active symptoms with prodromal or residual phases, or continuous signs for 6 months)
